chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said to his son al-Hasan (peace be upon him):

O my son, learn four things and (a further) four things from me. Nothing will harm you if you practise them: That the richest of riches is intelligence; the biggest destitution is foolishness; the wildest wildness is vanity and the best achievement is goodness of the moral character.
ai.seo_question: What are the four key virtues Imam Ali advised his son to remember?
ai.summary: In this famous hadith from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) presents a metaphysical redefinition of human values, contrasting intellectual depth (al-aql) with moral character (husn al-khuluq) as the true measures of wealth and nobility. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on the integration of reason and ethics, where 'vanity' (al-ujb) is identified as the root of spiritual isolation, distinct from mere social loneliness. By anchoring these virtues in the concept of 'aql' (intellect), the Imam aligns with the broader Islamic tradition that views rational understanding as the foundation for righteous action.
